replies.author: ShippingGuy15
replies.body:
Well, I personally spent hours and hours just studying the chart and tried to understand how it moved.  You can look for consistent patterns and see how they play out, use tools like the fibinocci or an indicator. 

Really the only thing I can say with certainty is that there’s no short cut, or one way to do it.  Anyone can make money pretty much any way as long as they put enough time and effort into their strategy and manage the mental and money side appropriately.  

There’s a reason why very few people actually make it in this game, and that’s with some people spending hundreds/thousands of hours doing this, and still can’t make money.

comments.author: Good_Character_20
comments.body: Your instinct is mostly right. The AI day trades and prints money content is almost all slop, and the tell is it's always selling something. An AI predicting the next candle and trading it live doesn't hold up, the signal to noise at that timeframe is brutal and the model mostly just learns the noise. Where AI actually helps is one step back in the research, things like generating ideas, writing and stress-testing backtests faster, and catching your own overfitting. That part is real and boring and nobody makes a viral video about it. On passing an eval specifically, that's survivorship. An eval is a risk test, and if a hundred bots each push toward the profit target, a few pass by luck and post it while the ninety-something that breached drawdown stay quiet. You're seeing the winners of a coin-flip tournament, not proof the AI can trade.

comments.author: silphotographer
comments.body:
That's like asking if the wrench can do repairs. 

AI doesn't rationalize or think. AI is merely automation tool. AI cannot produce a strategy for  you. It has to either take your context or it will navigate internet and find whatever context that is best fit for its algo (whether it's correct or has real edge or not). 

In my case, LLM did not derive a system with edge, but it was able to generate some meaningful input that I took to optimize it a bit better.
